question: Does the proposed seven-orbit source admit a weight- and damping-independent site-response falsification test?
assumptions: The C3-labeled seven-cell source represents the physical additive site-to-lateral coupling.
Vertical site variables and the lateral direct basis have independently established physical registration.
A conventional material cross-Hessian, if present, must be independently subtracted before testing an added UD source.
physical_mapping: HYPOTHESIS: abstract 14-site source to graphite atom/phonon displacement-force cross Hessian; registration and scale require independent calibration
target_exposure: The paired angles and weak-load response were known before source selection; this calculation uses neither as a fit. The KC model and offset 2 were previously exposed development inputs.
fitted_choices: No new parameters fit; replay uses previously selected C3 alignment offset 2 and bond length 1.42 Angstrom from archived calculation
baseline: Full C3-equivariant eight-dimensional coupling space and independently registered conventional PES/cross Hessian
result: EXACT/CONDITIONAL: two explicit linear null tests are necessary and sufficient for membership in the pure six-dimensional seven-orbit source span within C3-equivariant maps. NUMERICAL/DEVELOPMENT: five archived KC cross Hessians violate the pure-source constraints; no measurement uncertainty or independent empirical inference.
next_discriminant: Measure four representative site cross-Hessian columns and covariance after independent conventional baseline subtraction and C3 registration; then constrain damping from separate data
